subject: ACME: sudden p99/429 surge — immediate mitigation and exec note
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 19:05:00 +0000
Subject: High p99 / 429 flood impacting nightly ingestion

Hi Neha,

We're seeing a pretty severe degradation in the last 48 hours on calls to /v1/generate for our ingestion pipeline. p95 is elevated (~500ms -> 1.2s) and p99 is spiking to 4-6s; more concerningly, we are getting a burst of 429s that seems correlated with the high token counts in certain batched requests. The 429s are cascading into retries from our side which then amplify the tail latency — it's basically a feedback loop.

Impact: throughput dropped ~30% during peak windows (09:00-11:30 PT), and timeouts are creeping into our downstream ETL (we had 3 failed ingestion jobs overnight). This is customer-impacting for two of our freemium ingestion pipelines.

I've attached a small bundle with request samples and a short trace. Can we get an urgent remediation path and an executive note I can show to my CTO? Also need a short-term tweak so our job runs don't keep retrying into the flood.

Available for an emergency call — Jordan (PST office hours).

Thanks,
Jordan
Head of Integrations, ACME

Attachments: acme-request-samples.json (json), sample-429-trace.log (text)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 19:23:00 +0000
Subject: Re: High p99 / 429 flood impacting nightly ingestion

Jordan — thanks for the details and the samples. I'm very sorry for the disruption. We're treating this as a P1.

Immediate steps (next 2 hours):
- Rishi and SRE will run a quick correlation to identify whether the 429s are coming from per-request concurrency or token-rate enforcement and share a mitigation.
- Temporary per-customer token cap (soft) and a conservative circuit-breaker policy for ACME to prevent retry amplification.
- We can also increase your quota window for the short term if you want to avoid blocking while we stabilize.

Proposed 30-min war-room at 20:00 UTC (we can move if needed). Sean, can you join for comms and commercial ask?

I'll follow up with a brief exec summary for your CTO right after the call.

— Neha
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: High p99 / 429 flood impacting nightly ingestion

On Thu, Apr 8, 2027 at 19:23, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com> wrote:
> Jordan — thanks for the details and the samples. I'm very sorry for the disruption. We're treating this as a P1.

Quick triage summary (SRE):
- Correlated your sample trace with server logs: spikes line up with several large-batch requests (token counts > 12k) arriving within short windows.
- Our per-request rate limiter currently uses requests/sec and connection concurrency; it doesn't cap token-rate directly. Large requests consume disproportionate GPU time and can push queue lengths up, causing >429s and higher scheduling latency.
- Retries from client-side are producing bursts that inflate queue depth and push p99 higher — classic retry amplification.

Short-term mitigations (rolling out now):
1) Soft token-rate cap: throttle requests above 6k tokens to a 1 req/s max for ACME via customer policy (no hard cut, 429 with Retry-After of 8s).
2) Aggressive retry headers: emit Retry-After + guidance in 429 body; set advisory header X-Redwood-Backoff: token.
3) Circuit-breaker: temporary 30s open for a customer if error rate > 15% in a 1m window.
4) Route heavy-token traffic to warm warm-pool of dedicated capacity (if ACME approves temporary bump).

Medium-term (48–72h):
- Implement token-aware rate limiter in the control plane (token-budget accounting).
- Add early-shed for very long sequences (return a 413 or a structured hint to chunk).

I'll post the exact log slices and a short dashboard to the drive link.

Rishi
SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: acme-observability-snaps.zip (metrics), sample-429-trace.log (detailed)

Neha: I'll prepare an exec-level note for your CTO summarizing what we've done and the commitments (mitigation, timeline, credits).

Sean

Jordan
